claim: Full sharding (FSDP/ZeRO-3) costs 1.5x the communication overhead and volume of DDP when using a bandwidth-optimal ring algorithm.
stance_target: the repo's claim that FSDP moves ~1.5x the bytes of DDP, and refutes research.md's ~2x multiplier
scope_conditions: Ring-algorithm collectives; full sharding factor F = world size; any interconnect
quoted_support: The full sharding strategy leads to the lowest memory footprint but incurs the most communication overhead, for example, full sharding has 1.5x communication overhead and volume over DDP if using bandwidth optimal ring algorithm.

claim: DDP requires all model parameters, gradients and optimizer states to fit on a single device, so models above roughly one billion parameters OOM on a 40 GB GPU.
stance_target: the premise that DDP's viability is bounded by per-card model-state capacity, which is what Memory Grafting's frozen tables are meant to relieve
scope_conditions: 40 GB GPU, mixed-precision Adam, models >1B parameters
quoted_support: For example, when training models with more than one billion parameters using a 40GB GPU device, DDP will likely encounter out-of-memory errors on each device.

claim: FSDP matches DDP throughput on models that fit (611M and 2.28B) and only diverges when DDP runs out of memory.
stance_target: the claim that sharding is a memory play, not a throughput win, at small model sizes
scope_conditions: T5-611M and T5-2.28B on A100-80GB; FSDP full sharding vs DDP
quoted_support: The performance of FSDP and DDP is similar when evaluating 611M and 2.28B models. However, DDP encounters an out-of-memory error when attempting to wrap models larger than 2.28B.

claim: FSDP's hybrid sharding strategy (1 < F < W) keeps shard groups inside a node to exploit higher intra-node bandwidth instead of paying inter-node costs.
stance_target: the claim that sharding topology should be matched to the fabric hierarchy, which on a 5-GPU PCIe box means a single flat group
scope_conditions: Multi-node clusters with a bandwidth hierarchy; sharding factor between 1 and world size
quoted_support: Hybrid sharding occurs when the sharding factor ranges between 1 and W. ... The remainder of this section focuses on full sharding and hybrid sharding since the full replication strategy is similar to the existing DDP.

claim: Setting the FSDP sharding factor to 1 degenerates exactly to vanilla data parallelism using AllReduce for gradient reduction.
stance_target: the equivalence between FSDP(F=1) and DDP, relevant to whether FSDP is 'a different topology' or just DDP plus optional sharding
quoted_support: By setting the sharding factor to 1, FSDP fully replicates the model and simplifies to vanilla data parallelism that uses AllReduce for gradient reduction.

claim: FSDP's native mixed precision permits running all collectives in low precision, which reduces communication volume.
stance_target: the claim that bf16 collectives (bf16_compress_hook or FSDP mixed precision) halve gradient traffic on a bandwidth-starved fabric
scope_conditions: FSDP native mixed precision with FP16 or BF16 low precision and FP32 full precision
quoted_support: Moreover, FSDP's mixed precision permits running all collectives in the low precision, which saves communication volume.
numbers: K_low bytes per low-precision element vs K_full per full-precision element

claim: FSDP's mixed-precision design cuts the transient unsharded-parameter peak from K_full*max(psi) to K_low*max(psi) bytes by keeping only the local shard resident and materializing the full FlatParameter on demand.
stance_target: the memory-budget claim that sharded training's peak is set by the largest unit, not the whole model
scope_conditions: N FlatParameters with numels psi_1..psi_N; sharding factor F
quoted_support: In other words, FSDP directly reduces the second K_full max_N psi_i term to K_low max_N psi_i.

claim: Backward prefetching of the next FSDP unit's parameters yields about 18% speedup on GPT-175B and the gain persists across cluster sizes.
stance_target: the claim that communication-computation overlap is the main lever for hiding collective cost on slow fabrics
quoted_support: Results are presented in Figure 6 (b), where pre-fetching leads to approximately 18% speedup, and this TFLOPS gain persists across different GPU cluster sizes.

claim: GPT-175B under FSDP reaches 173-186 TFLOPS/GPU against a 312 TFLOPS BF16 tensor-core peak and scales linearly from 128 to 512 GPUs.
stance_target: the reference point for what fraction of peak a well-overlapped sharded job achieves (~55-60%), useful for sanity-checking the repo's 810-TFLOPS aggregate assumption
quoted_support: With the 175B model, the experiments achieved more than 173 ... and 186 TFLOPS per GPU with batch size equal to 1 and 2 respectively ... peak is 312 TFLOPS using the BF16 tensor core.

claim: Combining FSDP with pipeline parallelism requires non-default sharding settings, because full sharding would unshard parameters once per micro-batch and cause significant communication overhead.
stance_target: the claim that PP+FSDP composition needs care on a bandwidth-limited fabric (relevant to the ZeroPP-style TP-free recipe)
scope_conditions: FSDP wrapping each pipeline stage; default full sharding; multiple micro-batches
quoted_support: However, as pipeline parallel divides input mini-batches into smaller micro-batches, the default full sharding strategy in FSDP would have to unshard model parameters for every micro-batch. Consequently, combining these approaches with default FSDP configurations may lead to significant communication overhead.
numbers: 1 AllGather per micro-batch under default FSDP

claim: In 2D TP+FSDP parallelism, PyTorch keeps tensor-parallel collectives intra-node to exploit higher bandwidth and puts FSDP collectives on the inter-node mesh dimension.
stance_target: the claim that TP is bandwidth-hungry enough to be confined to the fastest available links, which on a PCIe-only box means TP has no fast tier to live on
scope_conditions: PyTorch DTensor 2D mesh; TP on one dimension, FSDP on the other
quoted_support: We usually keep the tensor-parallel communications, which block subsequent computation, intra-node to leverage the higher network bandwidth, and allow the FSDP communications operate on the other mesh dimension inter-node.

claim: FSDP cannot guarantee mathematical equivalence with local training for optimizers that depend on unsharded parameter values (e.g. vector norms or second-order approximations).
stance_target: a correctness caveat for any FSDP-based experiment on the box
scope_conditions: Optimizer steps operating on FlatParameter shards that do not respect individual parameter boundaries
quoted_support: As a result, any optimizer computation that depends on an original parameter's unsharded value (e.g. vector norm), its tensor structure (e.g. approximate second-order optimizers), or require global states over all parameters will become invalid.

claim: FSDP's rate limiter on collective launches only helps when the CPU thread outruns the CUDA streams and causes allocator fragmentation; it gave no speedup on RegNet and hurt DeepViT.
stance_target: the claim that comm throttling is not a general-purpose fix for slow-fabric training
scope_conditions: RegNet 9B, T5-11B, DeepViT 8B on 2 and 4 nodes
quoted_support: One notable observation is that the rate limiter's effectiveness is not consistent, as it does not attain any speedups in the RegNet experiments, and even impedes the DeepViT ones.

claim: FSDP evaluation ran on A100-80GB GPUs interconnected by a 2 Tb/s RoCE network, i.e. the paper's throughput results assume a fabric far faster than PCIe Gen2 x4.
stance_target: the transferability limit of FSDP's published throughput numbers to a PCIe Gen2 x4, no-P2P box
quoted_support: the dense parameters were trained using FSDP on 8 to 512 A100 80GB GPUs interconnected by a 2Tb/s RoCE network.
